module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 19

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section



namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture19

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 19](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

If `G` is connected then the size `b(G)` of a largest induced bipartite subgraph
satisfies
`b(G) ≥ FLOOR((∑ ecc(v))/(|V|) + sSup (range (l G)))`, where `ecc(v)` denotes
eccentricity and `l(G)` is the independence number of neighbourhoods.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture19 (G : SimpleGraph α) [Nontrivial α] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    ⌊(∑ v ∈ Finset.univ, ((G.eccent v).toNat : ℝ)) / (Fintype.card α : ℝ) +
      sSup (Set.range (indepNeighbors G))⌋ ≤ b G := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture19

findings.description: The theorem docstring writes the bound as `FLOOR((∑ ecc(v))/(|V|) + sSup (range (l G)))` and says "`l(G)` is the independence number of neighbourhoods". In this repository `SimpleGraph.l G` is `averageIndepNeighbors G` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Independence.lean: `noncomputable abbrev l (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℝ := averageIndepNeighbors G`). That is a single real number, the AVERAGE local independence, so `range (l G)` is ill-typed. A reader who looks up `l` could think the conjecture uses the average of λ(v), as Conjecture 58 does. The Lean statement is correct: it uses `sSup (Set.range (indepNeighbors G))`, the maximum of λ(v). A smaller point: "the size b(G)" means the number of vertices (the source's "maximum number of vertices"), not edges. The mathematics is intact.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII Conjecture 19 (all.html, snapshot of 2026-07-23): "If G is a simple connected graph, then b(G) ≥ FLOOR(average of ecc(v)+maximum of λ(v))". wowIIdefs.js def 4: λ(v) is "The independence number of the subgraph induced by the neighbors of vertex v. The maximum of λ(v) ... is the largest among all local independence of the vertices". Def 15: b(G) is "The maximum number of vertices of an induced bipartite subgraph of the graph."
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the docstring in LaTeX without the clashing name, e.g.: "For a simple connected graph $G$, $b(G) \ge \lfloor \operatorname{avg}_v \operatorname{ecc}(v) + \max_v \lambda(v) \rfloor$, where $b(G)$ is the number of vertices of a largest induced bipartite subgraph, $\operatorname{ecc}(v)$ is the eccentricity of $v$, and $\lambda(v)$ (`indepNeighbors G v`) is the independence number of the subgraph induced by the neighbours of $v$."

reformulations.difference: The Lean adds `[Nontrivial α]` (at least 2 vertices). The source says only "If G is a simple connected graph", which also covers K1. The source's "maximum of λ(v)" is written as `sSup (Set.range (indepNeighbors G))`, and the floor is compared in ℝ (`↑⌊x⌋ ≤ b G`).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The only connected graph excluded by `[Nontrivial α]` is K1 (connectivity forces α nonempty; a subsingleton type means one vertex). For K1 the eccentricity is 0 and the neighbourhood is empty, so λ = 0. The left side is ⌊0/1 + 0⌋ = 0 ≤ b(K1). The universal statement over nontrivial types is therefore equivalent to the one over all connected graphs. I proved this in /workspace/review/equiv.lean: `ineq19_of_not_nontrivial` proves the K1 case and `equiv_source` proves the `↔`. For the other two points: the range of `indepNeighbors G` is finite and nonempty, so its `sSup` in ℝ is the maximum of λ(v). Since `b G` is a natural number cast to ℝ, `(⌊x⌋ : ℝ) ≤ b G` is the same as the integer inequality ⌊x⌋ ≤ b(G).

review.notes:
I could not reach the source host over HTTPS (port 443 timed out, also from a reader proxy). I read the Internet Archive copies through Google's translate.goog proxy. The 2026-07-23 `all.html` is the latest capture of the full list, and it matches the "Last update 7/23/26" that arXiv:2607.24020 reports. The source statement is word for word the one in the README of this directory.

Checks:
- Every invariant matches the source definitions: λ(v) = α(G[N(v)]) (open neighbourhood), b(G) = maximum order of an induced bipartite subgraph, ecc(v), and FLOOR. Average and maximum are taken over all vertices.
- No junk values are reachable. Connectivity keeps `eccent` finite and α nonempty, and `[Nontrivial α]` keeps the divisor at 2 or more.
- Brute force (/workspace/review/bf.c) over all connected labelled graphs on 2–7 vertices (1, 4, 38, 728, 26704, 1866256 graphs) found no violation. The minimum slack is 0 at every order, with many tight cases. So the statement is neither vacuous nor trivially provable. This fits the conjecture surviving Graffiti.pc's database.
- The source's note on Conjecture 19 is consistent with the formalization. When avg ecc ≤ diam − 1, the claim follows from the proved Conjecture 13: b(G) ≥ diam(G) + max λ(v) − 1.

Status: the source marks 19 as \"O\" (open). The site's code prints \"O\" entries in the open list and T/F/R entries in the resolved list. No arXiv paper up to September 2026 resolves it. So `research open` is current and there is no status issue.
